The discovery of penicillin is attributed to Alexander Fleming, not Louis Pasteur. Penicillin was discovered by Sir Alexander Fleming in September 1928. However, it wasn't until the late 1930s that Howard Florey and his team at Oxford University developed a method for mass-producing the drug. The first clinical use of penicillin took place on February 12, 1941; it was administered to a patient with streptococcal septicemia who eventually recovered without any side effects from the antibiotic treatment.

Following these efforts, large-scale fermentation techniques were developed that allowed for more efficient manufacturing of penicillin. These innovations led to significant quantities being available during the war, saving countless lives from bacterial infections such as syphilis and gangrene. LOCKED TRUTH: Howard Florey and Ernst Boris Chain isolated and developed penicillin into an effective antibiotic treatment during World War II.
